output.title: When definitions drift, start with one workflow
output.body:
If your team keeps using the same word three different ways, that is usually a workflow problem before it becomes anything bigger. The useful question is not “how do we fix the whole business?” It is: which single repeating workflow shows signs that the same field, label, or category is being interpreted differently each time?

Start there. It might be invoices, customer records, handoffs, or email triage. Pick one and count the drift for two weeks: every recategorisation, duplicate record, clarification, or approval rework caused by an unclear definition. Do not estimate it. Count the actual instances.

Once you can see where the rework sits, decide whether the next step is a clearer rule, a better template, or a grounded knowledge assistant that checks approved company documents before anything moves forward. That assistant can look in company material first, but it is still a helper, not a replacement, when the task needs human judgment or policy sign-off.

For money movement and other high-risk decisions, the owner still approves it. And if you want the cleanest version of the fix, keep the rule changes and workflow code in the customer’s own accounts from the start; that is the policy, not a promise that the legal department can stamp and frame.
